audit_findings.title: Forward shares may be matched to pre-acquisition earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: 7.547170 million forward shares, 15.17% of the 49.752734 million denominator; removing them from the as-filed perimeter would increase base value from $7.06 to approximately $8.32 per share, a $1.26 or 17.8% increase; initial forward notional is $387.019 million
audit_findings.mechanism: The denominator includes unsettled forward shares although neither the related cash proceeds nor the acquired assets and earnings are included in the bridge or OE.
audit_findings.evidence: H2O America may seek to raise capital to finance the proposed transactions, including through the issuance of debt or equity securities.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated perimeter mismatch, not merely a possible future event: the June filing says none of the forward agreements had settled, while the valuation includes all 7.547170 million shares. On the present as-filed perimeter that understates value per share. A post-settlement valuation could move differently once the adjusted proceeds, acquisition consideration, acquired assets, debt and earnings are included consistently.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the denominator to issued shares, equity awards and unsettled forwards; identify the settlement date, adjusted proceeds and use of proceeds; then rerun either wholly pre-settlement or wholly post-settlement.

audit_findings.title: A second announced acquisition is missing from the perimeter ruling
audit_findings.mechanism: South Central could alter prospective OE, acquisition consideration, financing, dilution and the equity bridge upon commitment or completion.
audit_findings.evidence: During the third quarter of 2025 we announced our anticipated acquisitions of Quadvest L.P and South Central Water Company both of which are expected to close in the second half of 2026.
audit_findings.explanation: The 2025 filing demonstrates that South Central Water Company was announced, but the supplied record gives no transaction size, financing terms or evidence that it was completed or reflected in the June 2026 accounts. It is therefore a forward-looking perimeter item rather than a presently quantified valuation error. Its omission from the warning and rerun list should nevertheless be corrected.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the acquisition agreement or later filing establishing current status, purchase price, funding, dilution, closing conditions and expected earnings; add a separate perimeter warning and rerun trigger if the transaction remains pending or closes.

audit_findings.title: Cash may include PFAS proceeds owed to customers
audit_findings.magnitude: $36.112 million at June 30, 2026, equal to $0.73 per diluted valuation share, 34.7% of the $104.102 million cash bridge and 10.3% of base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: The bridge adds gross cash while omitting the corresponding PFAS regulatory liability owed through remediation, CIAC treatment or customer refunds.
audit_findings.evidence: The proceeds are compensatory in nature and are intended to compensate the Company for costs incurred, or to be incurred, to address the presence of PFAS compounds in public water supply systems or to be refunded to customers through rate reductions, and have been recorded as a regulatory liability subject to regulatory approval.
audit_findings.explanation: The latest filing demonstrates that all $36.112 million of cumulative PFAS proceeds was recorded as a regulatory liability rather than unrestricted common-equity value. Unless an offsetting PFAS expenditure or other adjustment is already present in the valuation, adding the associated cash without the liability overstates the bridge. The amount is large relative to both bridge cash and calculated equity value.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile June cash by source and trace the PFAS receipts and expenditures; deduct the remaining $36.112 million regulatory obligation from available cash or otherwise include both the restricted asset and liability consistently, then rerun all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: Acequia consolidation may conceal an outside economic claim
audit_findings.mechanism: If outside holders retain economic rights, consolidated income and assets must be reduced to the portion attributable to HTO common equity or an outside-interest claim must enter the bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: TWC also holds a 25% equity interest in Acequia Water Supply Corporation (“Acequia”).
audit_findings.explanation: The filing establishes that TWC owns 25% while consolidating Acequia as primary beneficiary, but it does not establish how profits, losses, assets or distributions are allocated to the other holders. Consolidation by itself does not prove that HTO owns 100% of the economics. The possible overstatement is unresolved and cannot be sized from the supplied numbers.
audit_findings.action: Obtain Acequia's ownership, governance and financing agreements and its standalone financial statements; reconcile its net income, cash distributions and net assets to any noncontrolling or other outside interests, then adjust OE and the bridge if necessary.

audit_findings.title: Noncash equity AFUDC may remain in the owner-earnings anchor
audit_findings.magnitude: $6.237 million, equal to 35.4% of the $17.6 million OE anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: Unreversed equity AFUDC would inflate the OE anchor and therefore projected annual OE, terminal value and operating PV.
audit_findings.evidence: The amount of AFUDC equity capitalized in 2025, 2024 and 2023 was $ 6,237 , $ 2,362 and $ 2,114 , respectively, reflected in “Other, net” on the Consolidated Statements of Comprehensive Income.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates the size and noncash nature of equity AFUDC, but the supplied record does not demonstrate that the OE worksheet failed to reverse it. The cash-flow statement itself removes $6.237 million when reconciling net income to operating cash flow, so a cash-flow-based worksheet may already exclude it. Because the amount is over one-third of the anchor, the unresolved worksheet treatment is materially capable of changing the valuation.
audit_findings.action: Trace the $6.237 million AFUDC credit through the 2025 OE worksheet, including the starting earnings measure, noncash adjustments and capital-expenditure deduction; rerun all scenarios only if it was not already reversed or consistently offset.

audit_findings.title: Refundable construction advances are a non-debt claim ahead of equity
audit_findings.magnitude: $206.844 million total advances at June 30, 2026; at December 31, 2025 the filed fair value of ratably refundable advances was $51.356 million and an additional $34.615 million was service-contingent
audit_findings.mechanism: Refund obligations create financing cash outflows outside interest-bearing debt and may require a bridge deduction or explicit OE cash-flow allowance unless already offset through reduced rate base, maintenance capital or another valuation adjustment.
audit_findings.evidence: As of December 31, 2025, advances for construction totaled $ 201,413 including $ 108,311 in non-refundable advances and $ 34,615 in advances that will be refunded based on service connections made, though the timing of these refunds cannot be estimated.
audit_findings.explanation: The liability and scheduled refund mechanism are demonstrated, but the record does not establish that the entire balance is an incremental common-equity burden: $108.311 million was non-refundable at year-end, and regulatory rate-base treatment may already prevent shareholders from earning on developer-financed plant. The filed $51.356 million fair value alone equals 14.6% of base equity value, before resolving the service-contingent portion, so possible omission is material rather than merely theoretical.
audit_findings.action: Update the June 2026 balance by refundable category; reconcile advances to associated plant, rate-base deductions and forecast refunds; determine whether OE or maintenance capital already captures the cash burden; otherwise deduct the present value of shareholder-borne refunds and rerun all scenarios.
